findings.title: forgiveness promise becomes direct prayer
findings.claim: The opening continuation carries the speech from the promise to seek forgiveness into a direct act of prayer.
findings.mechanism: The supplied discourse boundary places the first-person invocation after the forgiveness promise, while the following movement supplies an answer to the declared separation.
findings.reader_payoff: The ayah becomes a move from hoped-for intercession to enacted withdrawal and direct address.
findings.containment: This is a local discourse handoff; it does not claim that the following movement proves the speaker's motive or replace the plain withdrawal.

findings.title: first-person calling has a named addressee
findings.claim: The first-person form is directed invocation of a named Lord rather than an open-ended call.
findings.mechanism: The explicit object follows the first-person imperfect and fixes the direction of the calling on a named addressee.
findings.reader_payoff: The speaker's calling is heard as purposeful prayer, not merely as speech or summoning.
findings.containment: The finding concerns the local object relation and does not exclude other ordinary senses of the calling root elsewhere.

findings.title: same act-class reversed by object and subject

findings.mechanism: The parallel second-person and first-person imperfects share the calling action, but their surrounding object relations reverse its direction.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast becomes a question of where calling is directed, not whether one side calls and the other does not.
findings.containment: The parallel does not deny the addressees' calling; it distinguishes its object and direction from Ibrahim's invocation.

epistemic.reason: The parallel grammar and explicit complements are directly supported in the packet.

findings.title: attributed prayer keeps the speaker from hardship
findings.claim: The attributed trace makes the hoped-for non-wretched state relational: sustained invocation of the nurturing Lord is presented as the way the speaker hopes not to enter hardship.
findings.mechanism: The exact focus trace contacts calling, step-by-step lordly care, the speaker's state of being, and hardship at the supplied word coordinates, so the hoped-for outcome is predicated of the speaker's condition.
findings.reader_payoff: Prayer's success becomes perceptible not only as receiving an object but as remaining in a relation that keeps the speaker from a condition of hardship.
findings.containment: This is attributed HFT evidence with legacy-unbound provenance; it preserves the ordinary request for relief, does not promise an answer, and does not invent an independent branch gloss.

epistemic.reason: The trace has an exact supplied focus anchor and complete coordinates, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and target morphology is not independently supplied.
